LESSON: POSITION AND SIZE OF COUNTRIES IN EASTERN AFRICA

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and the Built Environments Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Afr
Topic 1.1: Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do you determine the position of countries in Eastern Africa?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the countries of Eastern Africa on a map
2. describe the position and size of countries in Eastern Africa
3. use latitudes and longitudes to locate places on a map
4. appreciate the unity of Eastern African countries

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: POSITION AND SIZE OF COUNTRIES IN EASTERN AFRICA
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: POSITION AND SIZE OF COUNTRIES IN EASTERN AFRICA
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Identify the countries of Eastern Africa on a map

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the countries of Eastern Africa on a map. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the countries of Eastern Africa on a map.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the countries of Eastern Africa on a map. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe the position and size of countries in Eastern Africa

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the position and size of countries in Eastern Africa. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the position and size of countries in Eastern Africa.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the position and size of countries in Eastern Africa. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Use latitudes and longitudes to locate places on a map

What this means
In this part you learn to use latitudes and longitudes to locate places on a map. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use latitudes and longitudes to locate places on a map.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use latitudes and longitudes to locate places on a map. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate the unity of Eastern African countries

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the unity of Eastern African countries. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the unity of Eastern African countries.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the unity of Eastern African countries. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: identify the countries of Eastern Africa on a map)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa. (skill: describe the position and size of countries in Eastern Africa)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: use latitudes and longitudes to locate places on a map)

Example 4: Connect “Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: appreciate the unity of Eastern African countries)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the countries of Eastern Africa on a map.
3. Practise this skill: describe the position and size of countries in Eastern Africa.
4. Practise this skill: use latitudes and longitudes to locate places on a map.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you determine the position of countries in Eastern Africa?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the countries of Eastern Africa on a map.
5. Be able to: describe the position and size of countries in Eastern Africa.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
